question.knowledge_point: Identifying Extrema of a Function Given Its Graph
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980112/assets/d9d8fb6d663d8dfd0cce24ae3817c936e2e97ab2df7aefeaa0c734caf0311b94.png)

The graph of $y=f(x)$ is plotted above. Given that $f(x)$ is defined on the interval $x\in [-3,10]$, which points represent the global maximum of $f(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
The global extrema of a function are the lowest or highest points of the function's graph over its entire domain.

The lowest point is the global minimum, whereas the highest point is the global maximum.

According to the graph, the highest points are $B$ and $D$, and so these points represents the global maximum of $f(x).$
